pages.title: Abraham and the Idols
pages.content:
A very long time ago, a boy was born in the kingdom of Babylon in Mesopotamia. His parents named him Abraham. Abraham was an honest and intelligent boy. He loved Allah more than anything. When he grew up, Allah made him His great Messenger. People in Abraham’s town did not know Allah. They did not worship Him. They bowed to the stars, the moon, the sun, and stone objects. These objects looked like people or animals.

People believed these objects were their gods. They even made a special house for them. They came to the house, talked to the stone gods, and made a wish. Abraham thought that was silly. He was a smart boy. He saw that the stone objects did not eat, drink, or talk. They could not move from one place to another, and they could not hear or understand their wishes!

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:abraham-babylon
__historical_entity__:abraham-mesopotamia
A person chosen by Allah to tell people what He wants.
To pray to and show great love and respect to God or a god.
Always telling the truth.
Something that a person hopes will happen.

hotspots.title: Babylon
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) was born in the kingdom of Babylon in Mesopotamia.

hotspots.title: Stone Gods
hotspots.description: People believed that stone objects were their gods.

exercises.title: Silly Wishes
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: People talked to the stone gods. Why did Abraham think that was silly?
options: The people made the stone gods angry with their many wishes.
The stone objects could not hear or understand the wishes.
The special house of the stone gods was far from his town.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says Abraham saw that the stone objects “did not eat, drink, or talk” and “could not hear or understand their wishes!”

feedback.correct: Yes! The stone objects could not hear or understand. So making wishes to them was silly.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the last sentences of Chapter 1 again. What could the stone objects not do?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Looked Like” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 1. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “These objects looked like people or animals.” What does this sentence mean?
options: The objects were real people or animals in the town.
The objects had the shape of people or animals.
The objects liked people and animals very much.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Look like + noun” tells us about shape or appearance. The objects had the shape of people or animals, but they were only stone. The next sentence tells us something different: “People believed these objects were their gods.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “Looked like” is about the shape of the objects. They were not real people or animals.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph again. Were the objects real people, or were they stone objects with that shape?

languageFocusExercises.title: Past Forms in the Story
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each verb with its past form from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the past form of each verb?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story happened “a very long time ago”, so the chapter uses past forms. These five verbs are irregular: they do not end in -ed. “When he grew up, Allah made him His great Messenger.” “Abraham thought that was silly.” “He saw that the stone objects did not eat, drink, or talk.” “They came to the house …”

feedback.correct: Well done. These past forms do not end in -ed, so it is good to learn them.
feedback.incorrect: Find each verb in Chapter 1: “grew up”, “made him”, “thought that”, “saw that”, “came to the house”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Did Not and Could Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which verb form comes after “did not” and “could not”?

formChoices.sentence: They did not [choice] Him.
He saw that the stone objects did not [choice], drink, or talk.
They could not [choice] from one place to another …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “did not” and “could not”, use the base verb: did not worship, did not eat, could not move. “Did not” tells a fact about the past. “Could not” tells us that someone or something was not able to do it.

feedback.correct: Correct. After “did not” and “could not”, the verb has no -ed and no -ing.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the end of each paragraph in Chapter 1. After “did not” and “could not”, use the base verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Belief and Observation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say three or four short sentences about the stone objects.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did the people believe, and what was true?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can use past-story verbs, “did not”, “could not” and “looked like” to contrast the people’s belief with Abraham’s observation.

feedback.correct: Use accurate Chapter 1 language to make the contrast clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what people believed: “People believed …”
discussionPrompts.example: People believed the stone objects were their gods.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what they did not do: “They did not …”
discussionPrompts.example: They did not know Allah, and they did not worship Him.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Describe the objects: “They looked like …”
discussionPrompts.example: The objects looked like people or animals.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what they could not do: “But they could not …”
discussionPrompts.example: But they could not move, hear or understand.

pages.title: Abraham and His Father
pages.content:
Abraham’s father was an idol maker. As a young boy, Abraham used to watch his father making idols from stone. One day, Abraham asked his father, “Why do you make and put these toys in the house?” His father said, “They are not toys. They are our gods. We show love and respect to them. We ask them for help and give them presents.”

But Abraham played with these idols as toys. He rode on their backs and sometimes kicked them. One day, his father saw Abraham. He was riding the king of the gods. He got angry and told his son not to play with it again. Abraham asked, “What is this human-like object, father? It has big ears. Its ears are bigger than ours.” His father answered, “It is Mardukh, the king of gods, son! He has big ears because he is very smart.” This made Abraham laugh; that was so ridiculous.

vocabulary.definition: A statue or object that people worship as a god.
The feeling that someone or something is important and should be treated well.
Very silly or not making sense.
Things given to someone as gifts.

hotspots.title: Idol Making
hotspots.description: The father of Abraham (pbuh) made idols from stone.

hotspots.title: Mardukh
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) laughed when his father said the idol Mardukh was very smart.

exercises.title: Mardukh’s Big Ears
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Why did Abraham laugh at his father’s words about Mardukh?
options: His father said Mardukh had big ears because Mardukh was very smart.
His father said the idols were just toys for the children.
His father said Mardukh gave the people presents and food every day.
exercises.explanation: His father said, “He has big ears because he is very smart.” Then the chapter says: “This made Abraham laugh; that was so ridiculous.” The father did not say the idols were toys: He said, “They are not toys.”

feedback.correct: Right! Big ears do not make a stone statue smart. That is why Abraham laughed.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 2 again. Find the father’s answer that starts with “It is Mardukh …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Again and Again, or One Time?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Did it happen again and again, or only one time?

items: But Abraham played with these idols as toys
One day, Abraham asked his father
One day, his father saw Abraham

Again and again: But Abraham played with these idols as toys
Only one time: One day, Abraham asked his father
One day, his father saw Abraham

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter first tells us about Abraham’s habits as a young boy: He played with the idols, rode on their backs and “sometimes” kicked them. “Sometimes” shows that it happened more than once. “One day” takes us to one special time in the story.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the habits from the one-time events.
feedback.incorrect: Look for “sometimes” and “One day” in Chapter 2. What did Abraham do many times? What happened on one day?

languageFocusExercises.title: Used To, Bigger Than, Because
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each sentence?

formChoices.sentence: As a young boy, Abraham used to [choice] his father making idols from stone.
Its ears are [choice] than ours.
He has big ears [choice] he is very smart.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Used to + base verb” (used to watch) tells us about a habit in the past. Short adjectives add -er to compare: big → bigger than. “Because” gives a reason: the father says the idol has big ears because it is very smart.

feedback.correct: Well done. You completed a habit, a comparison and a reason.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 2 again. After “used to”, use the base verb. To compare, say “bigger than”. Which word gives a reason?

languageFocusExercises.title: Telling Someone Not to Do Something
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to make the sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did the father tell Abraham?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The pattern is “tell + person + not to + base verb”: “He got angry and told his son not to play with it again.” The word “not” comes before “to play”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You built the sentence: told + person + not to + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the father’s feeling. Then say who he told, and then “not to play”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Ask, Compare and Explain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say three or four short sentences about the big idol.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you ask and talk about the idol?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can ask “What is ...?” or “Why ...?”, use “bigger than” to compare the ears, and use “because” to give a reason. It may also report the father’s instruction with “told ... not to ...”.

feedback.correct: Use the chapter patterns accurately and keep the exchange short and clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Ask about the object: “What is this …?”
discussionPrompts.example: What is this big stone object in the house?

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Compare: “Its ears are bigger than …”
discussionPrompts.example: Its ears are bigger than our ears.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a reason: “… because …”
discussionPrompts.example: Abraham laughed because a stone object cannot be smart.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 (if you like) — Say what his father told him: “His father told him not to …”
discussionPrompts.example: His father told him not to play with it again.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What was Abraham’s father’s job?
beforeYouRead.quote: Abraham’s father was an idol maker.

iCan: I can tell what Abraham did with the idols as a boy.
I can say what someone used to do and compare two things.
I can ask and answer short questions about an object.

pages.title: Abraham Looks at the Sky
pages.content:
He was only seven years old at that time. Years passed and Abraham grew up. He always thought about Allah. He wanted to know who created the world. He knew that Allah was not an object. He was sad to see the people in the kingdom; they were still worshipping stone gods. Abraham was in search of one true Creator.

One night, Abraham left his home and took a walk in the countryside. On a nearby mountain, he found a cave and sat there. He started thinking about Allah. Then, he stood up and looked at the beautiful sky. He saw a bright star and thought, “Could this be my Lord?” But when it disappeared, he said, “I will not show respect to it because it sets and disappears.” He then saw the shining moon and said, “Could this be my Lord?” But when the moon went away, he said, “Allah never goes away!” He understood that it could not be his Lord.

vocabulary.definition: The One who made everything.
The act of looking for something.
Went away and could not be seen any more.
Land with fields and farms outside towns and cities.

hotspots.title: The Star
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) saw a bright star and asked, “Could this be my Lord?”

hotspots.title: The Moon
hotspots.description: The moon also went away, so Abraham (pbuh) knew it could not be his Lord.

exercises.title: A Night of Thinking
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 3 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last that night?

sequencingItems.text: Abraham sat in a cave on a mountain.
Abraham saw a bright star in the sky.
The star disappeared.
Abraham saw the shining moon.
The moon went away, and he said, “Allah never goes away!”

exercises.explanation: Abraham found a cave on a nearby mountain and sat there. Then he saw a bright star, but it disappeared. Next he saw the shining moon. When the moon went away, he said, “Allah never goes away!”

feedback.correct: Great! You followed Abraham from the cave to the star and then to the moon.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the second paragraph step by step: First the cave, then the star, then the moon.

languageFocusExercises.title: A Question to Himself
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the question from Chapter 3. Choose what Abraham is doing.
languageFocusExercises.question: Abraham saw a bright star and thought, “Could this be my Lord?” What is Abraham doing?
options: He is sure that the star is his Lord.
He is telling the star what to do.
He is asking himself if it is possible.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Could this be …?” asks if something is possible. Abraham is not sure yet. He watches the star, and then he decides.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Could this be …?” is a question about what is possible.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the question mark and read what happens next in Chapter 3. Was Abraham sure at that moment?

languageFocusExercises.title: Thinking and Searching
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each Chapter 3 expression with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words tell us about Abraham’s thinking?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 3 shows Abraham’s mind at work: “He always thought about Allah. He wanted to know who created the world. … Abraham was in search of one true Creator.” Then the star “disappeared”: he could not see it any more.

feedback.correct: Well done. You understood the words about Abraham’s thinking and searching.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3 again. Which words show a thought, a wish to learn, and a search?

languageFocusExercises.title: Then, Because, Could Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank], he stood up and looked at the beautiful sky. … But when it disappeared, he said, “I will not show respect to it, [blank] it sets and disappears.” … He understood that it [blank] be his Lord.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Then” moves the story to the next action. “Because” gives the reason for Abraham’s words. “Could not be” shows his conclusion: It was not possible for the star or the moon to be his Lord.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used a sequence word, a reason word and a conclusion.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3 again. Which word gives the next action? Which word gives a reason? What did Abraham understand at the end?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Ask, Observe and Conclude
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say three or four short sentences about a small mystery.
languageFocusExercises.question: What could it be?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can use “Could this be ...?”, “When ...”, “because ...” and “It could/could not be ...” to move from a question to evidence and a conclusion.

feedback.correct: Keep the reasoning simple and make the link between the observation and conclusion clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Ask a question: “Could this be …?”
discussionPrompts.example: I heard a noise at the door and thought, “Could this be my brother?”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you saw: “When I …, I …”
discussionPrompts.example: When I opened the door, I saw only the wind.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a reason: “… because …”
discussionPrompts.example: It was not my brother because he was at school.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what you think: “It could / could not be …”
discussionPrompts.example: It could not be my brother; it was only the wind.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Why was Abraham sad?
beforeYouRead.quote: He was sad to see the people in the kingdom; they were still worshipping stone gods.

iCan: I can tell what Abraham saw in the night sky.
I can ask “Could this be …?” and give a reason.
I can think through a small mystery with a partner.

pages.title: Allah Guides Abraham
pages.content:
Abraham stayed all night. In the morning the sun came out. It was shining and very bright. When he saw the bright sun, he thought, “Could this be my Lord? It is bigger and brighter.” But when it set, he got the idea that Allah is not a creation. Allah is the Creator of everything. He takes care of us. He never leaves us alone.

Abraham put his forehead to the ground and spoke to Allah. He said, “If Allah doesn’t show me the right way, I will be on the wrong path.” Allah answered his prayer and made him His Messenger. From then on, he had to guide his people. Prophet Abraham (pbuh) went home and told his father, “O my father, follow me: I will guide you on the right way. Stop worshipping stones.” His father got angry and said, “Are you against my gods?”

vocabulary.definition: To show someone the right way to go.
Speaking to Allah and asking Him for help.
The part of the face above the eyes.
Full of strong light.

hotspots.title: The Setting Sun
hotspots.description: The sun set, so Abraham (pbuh) understood that it was only a creation.

hotspots.title: Prayer
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) put his forehead to the ground and prayed to Allah.

exercises.title: The Bright Sun
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 4.
exercises.question: The sun was bigger and brighter than the star and the moon. Why did Abraham decide it was not Allah?
options: His father told him to stop looking at the sky.
The moon came out again, and it was brighter.
It set, so it was only a creation.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says: “But when it set, he got the idea that Allah is not a creation. Allah is the Creator of everything.”

feedback.correct: Yes! The sun set like the star and the moon. It is a creation, and Allah is the Creator.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4 again. What happened to the sun, and what idea did Abraham get?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Had To” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 4. Then decide: True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “From then on, he had to guide his people.” True or false: Guiding his people was now Abraham’s duty.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Had to + base verb” tells us about a duty or something necessary in the past. Allah made Abraham His Messenger, so now guiding his people was his job.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Had to guide” means it was his duty to guide them.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of the second paragraph again. What happened just before this sentence? Allah “made him His Messenger”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Time Words in the Story
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which time words fit the gaps?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Abraham stayed [blank]. [blank] the sun came out. It was shining and very bright. [blank] he saw the bright sun, he thought, “Could this be my Lord? It is bigger and brighter.”
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “All night” tells us how long Abraham stayed: From evening until morning. We say “in the morning”, not “on the morning”. “When” joins two actions: First he saw the sun, then he had a new thought.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the time words to move the story forward.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first lines of Chapter 4 again. How long did Abraham stay? Which preposition goes with “the morning”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix Abraham’s words?

errorItems.sentence: He said, “If Allah will not show me the right way, I will be on the wrong path.”
“O my father, follow me: I will guide you on the right way. Stop worship stones.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “If”, use the present form, not “will”: “If Allah doesn’t show me …, I will be …”. “Will” goes in the result part. After “Stop”, use the -ing form: “Stop worshipping stones.”

feedback.correct: Correct. You fixed the if-sentence and the verb after “Stop”.
feedback.incorrect: Read Abraham’s prayer and his words to his father in Chapter 4. Which form comes after “If”? Which form comes after “Stop”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Condition, Duty and Guidance
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say three short sentences about your day.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you have to do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “If ... will ...”, “have to ...”, and an imperative such as “Follow ...” or “Stop ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences short and make each pattern clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what will happen: “If I …, I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: If I don’t go to bed early, I will be tired in the morning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you must do: “I have to …”
discussionPrompts.example: At home, I have to clean my room every week.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a short instruction: “Please …”
discussionPrompts.example: Please close the window.

options: The moon is bigger than the sun.

The night is longer than the day.
beforeYouRead.quote: Allah is the Creator of everything.

pages.title: Abraham Calls His People
pages.content:
His father said, “If you do not stop speaking like this, I will stone you. Leave here now.” Prophet Abraham (pbuh) was very sad about his father. Then, he went to the people of the kingdom. He was trying to show them the right way: “O people! I believe in Allah. I do not worship stone idols because Allah is the one and only God!” People were very angry when they heard him.

Abraham (pbuh) said to them, “Why do you bow down to these objects? They have no power to help you.” People said, “We saw our fathers worship them; because of this, we do the same.” Abraham (pbuh) told them, “My Lord gives me food and drink when I need them. He heals me when I am sick. Your gods have no power to do these things.” But people didn’t listen to him.

vocabulary.definition: Makes a sick person healthy again.
To accept that something is true.
The ability to do something.
To bend your body low to show respect or worship.

hotspots.title: One God
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) called the people to worship Allah alone.

hotspots.title: Allah Provides
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) explained that Allah gives food, drink, and healing.

exercises.title: Why Did They Worship?
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 5.
exercises.question: The people said they worshipped the idols because the idols gave them food and drink.
exercises.explanation: The people said, “We saw our fathers worship them; because of this, we do the same.” It was Abraham who said that Allah gives him food and drink.

feedback.correct: Correct! The people only followed their fathers. The idols had no power to give them anything.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5 again. Find the people’s answer with the words “because of this”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words from Abraham’s Talk
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each Chapter 5 expression with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 5 mean?

matchingPairs.right: paid no attention to his words

correctAnswer.didn’t listen to him: paid no attention to his words

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The father says, “Leave here now.” Abraham asks, “Why do you bow down to these objects?” He says Allah “heals me when I am sick”. At the end, “people didn’t listen to him”: they heard him, but they did not accept his words.

feedback.correct: Well done. You understood the key words of the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Find each expression in Chapter 5 and read the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Do or Does? Have or Has?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word goes with I, you and they?

formChoices.sentence: “O people! I believe in Allah. I [choice] worship stone idols …
“Why [choice] you bow down to these objects?
Your gods [choice] no power to do these things.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: With I, you, we, they and plural nouns, use “do not”, “do” and “have”: I do not worship, Why do you …?, Your gods have no power. With he, she and it, use “does” and “has”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right present form for each subject.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the subject of each sentence: I, you, your gods. Is it he/she/it, or not?

languageFocusExercises.title: Every Time I Need
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to build Abraham’s sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does Abraham say what Allah always does for him?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “When + present verb” shows something that happens every time: every time Abraham needs food and drink, Allah gives them to him. The chapter uses the same pattern in “He heals me when I am sick.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “When I need them” tells us every time this happens.
feedback.incorrect: Start with who gives, then what He gives, then “when” and the situation.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Belief, Reason and General Situations
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about something you believe.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you believe, and why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “I believe ...”, “because ...”, “When ...”, and “has/has no power to ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep each sentence simple and clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what you believe: “I believe that …”
discussionPrompts.example: I believe that reading every day is good for us.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give a reason: “… because …”
discussionPrompts.example: It is good because we learn new words.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what happens: “When I …, I …”
discussionPrompts.example: When I read before bed, I sleep well.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — End with: “… has / has no power to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My old phone has no power to play big games.

beforeYouRead.quote: People were very angry when they heard him.

pages.title: Abraham Breaks the Idols
pages.content:
Abraham (pbuh) wanted to show his people that it was so silly to love and talk to idols. He made a plan to break all their stone gods. But he did not tell anyone about his plan. There was a big festival soon. All the people went outside of town. He got an axe and waited. When the town was empty, he went into the big house full of human-like objects.

He saw all of them. They stood there. There were plates of food in front of them. Abraham (pbuh) jokingly asked them, “Why don’t you eat the food? It is getting cold.” Abraham (pbuh) began to break the stone gods, one after another. In the end, they were all broken. He left the largest one unbroken. Abraham (pbuh) placed the axe around its neck and hurried back home.

vocabulary.definition: A special time when people celebrate something.
A tool with a heavy blade, used for cutting or breaking things.
Still whole, with no damage.
Moved or went somewhere quickly.

hotspots.title: The Axe
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) took an axe and waited until the town was empty.

hotspots.title: The Largest Idol
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) broke the idols but left the largest one unbroken.

exercises.title: The Right Time
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 6.
exercises.question: When did Abraham go into the big house of the stone gods?
options: at night, after he looked at the moon and the stars
when all the people were outside the town for the festival
the next morning, together with his father and the other people
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “There was a big festival soon. All the people went outside of town.” Then, “When the town was empty, he went into the big house.”

feedback.correct: Right! The town was empty, so nobody could stop him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6 again. Where did all the people go?

languageFocusExercises.title: It Is Getting Cold
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Abraham’s words from Chapter 6. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: Abraham jokingly asked the idols, “Why don’t you eat the food? It is getting cold.” What does “It is getting cold” mean?
options: The food is becoming colder now.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Get + adjective” means “become”. “It is getting cold” shows a change that is happening now: The food is slowly becoming colder. Abraham says it as a joke because the idols cannot eat.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Is getting cold” shows a change happening now.
feedback.incorrect: Think about hot food on a plate. What happens to it when nobody eats it?

languageFocusExercises.title: Plans and Scenes
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each sentence about Abraham’s plan?

formChoices.sentence: Abraham (pbuh) wanted [choice] his people that it was so silly to love and talk to idols.
But he did not tell [choice] about his plan.
There [choice] plates of food in front of them.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “want”, use “to + base verb”: wanted to show. After “did not”, use “anyone”, not “someone” or “nobody”. Use “There were” for more than one thing (plates) and “There was” for one thing (“There was a big festival soon”).

feedback.correct: Well done. You completed the intention, the secret and the scene.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph and the start of the second paragraph of Chapter 6 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Step by Step
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the Chapter 6 sentences in the order they happened.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Abraham do first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: Abraham (pbuh) got an axe and waited.
When the town was empty, Abraham (pbuh) went into the big house …
Abraham (pbuh) began to break the stone gods, one after another.
In the end, they were all broken.
Abraham (pbuh) placed the axe around its neck and hurried back home.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter tells the plan step by step. “When the town was empty” shows the right time to act. “Began to break” is the start of the action, “one after another” shows that he broke them one by one, and “In the end” shows the result.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the plan from start to end.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the time words in Chapter 6: “When”, “began to”, “In the end”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Simple Plan and Sequence
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four or five short sentences about your plan.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you tell your plan step by step?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can use “wanted to ...”, “made a plan to ...”, “There was/were ...”, “When ...”, “began to ...”, and a sequence expression such as “one after another” or “In the end”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sequence clear and use each pattern for its real function.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what you wanted: “I wanted to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I wanted to surprise my mother with a cake.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say your plan: “I made a plan to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I made a plan to make the cake alone.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Set the scene: “There was / were …” or “When …”
discussionPrompts.example: When my mother went to the market, I went into the kitchen.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what you did: “I began to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I began to mix the eggs, the milk and the flour.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say how it ended: “In the end, …” or “one after another”
discussionPrompts.example: In the end, the cake was ready, and my mother was very happy.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Who did Abraham tell about his plan?
beforeYouRead.quote: But he did not tell anyone about his plan.

I can say what someone wanted to do, step by step.
I can describe a simple plan in four or five sentences.

pages.title: The People Question Abraham
pages.content:
The next day, people went to the house of gods. They were shocked because all their stone gods were in pieces. People came together around the pieces. They wondered and asked, “Who did this?” Some of them said, “We heard a young man; he spoke against our gods.” They remembered, “His name was Abraham.”

People found Abraham (pbuh) and brought him to the house of idols. They asked him, “Did you harm our gods?” Abraham (pbuh) calmly said, “It was this god there, the biggest one. It broke all the stones. Ask it if it can speak!” The people were displeased with his answer and said, “You know that these objects don’t speak!” Abraham (pbuh) said, “Then, why do you worship these objects? Don’t you see that they can’t speak or see or even protect themselves? Don’t you understand?”

vocabulary.definition: Very surprised and upset.
Unhappy or annoyed about something.
To keep someone or something safe.
To hurt someone or damage something.

hotspots.title: Broken Idols
hotspots.description: The people found their idols broken into pieces.

hotspots.title: Abraham’s Answer
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) told the people to ask the biggest idol if it could speak.

exercises.title: Ask the Biggest One
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: Abraham told the people, “Ask it if it can speak!” Why did he say this?
options: He really believed that the biggest idol was angry and broke all the other gods.
He wanted to take the biggest idol home and keep it in his father’s house.
He wanted the people themselves to see that their gods were only stone objects.
exercises.explanation: The people answered, “You know that these objects don’t speak!” Then Abraham asked, “Then, why do you worship these objects?” Their own answer showed the truth.

feedback.correct: Yes! The people said it themselves: The objects don’t speak. So why worship them?
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 7 again. What did the people answer, and what did Abraham ask next?

languageFocusExercises.title: Two Kinds of Questions
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each Chapter 7 question in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it a “Who? Why?” question, or a yes/no question?

items: Then, why do you worship these objects?

Has a question word (Who? Why?): Then, why do you worship these objects?

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Who …?” asks for a person and “Why …?” asks for a reason. Questions that start with “Don’t …?” or “Are …?” can have a yes/no answer. Abraham’s yes/no questions make the people think: They know the answer.

feedback.correct: Correct. You sorted the questions by their form.
feedback.incorrect: Look at each question. Does it have a question word like “Who” or “why”?

languageFocusExercises.title: The Next Day
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: When did the people come, and how did they feel?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank], people went to the house of gods. They were [blank] because all their stone gods were in pieces. … The people were displeased [blank] his answer …
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “The next day” moves the story to a new time. “Shocked” is a strong feeling of surprise; “because” gives the reason for it. We say “displeased with” something or someone.

feedback.correct: Well done. You completed the time, the feeling and the word after “displeased”.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 7 again. How did the people feel when they saw the pieces? Which word comes after “displeased”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the verbs in these lines?

errorItems.sentence: They asked him, “Did you harmed our gods?”
“It broke all the stones. Ask it if it can speaks!”
… and said, “You know that these objects doesn’t speak!”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “Did”, use the base verb: “Did you harm …?” After “can”, use the base verb: “can speak”. With a plural subject (these objects), use “don’t”, not “doesn’t”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You fixed all three verb forms.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 7 again. Look at the verb after “Did” and “can”, and at the subject “these objects”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Ask and Explain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four or five sentences about a small school mystery.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and who did it?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can use “The next day ...”, “Who ...?”, “Did you ...?”, “I know that ...”, “Ask ... if ...”, “can/can’t ...”, and “because ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the questions natural and use each pattern for its real function.

discussionPrompts.example: The next day, my pencil case was not on my desk.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Ask a question: “Who …?” or “Did you …?”

discussionPrompts.example: I found it under my chair because it fell from the desk.

pages.title: Abraham Is Thrown into the Fire
pages.content:
They felt ashamed and looked at each other because they knew Abraham was right. But they were too arrogant to accept their mistake. They started shouting, “Burn him! Burn him! In the name of our gods, punish him!” People of the kingdom collected firewood for the fire for days. The fire was so huge that it was dangerous to go near it. But Abraham (pbuh) stayed calm because he trusted Allah. Allah was always with him.

News about the fire traveled very fast and far. People from many different towns came to watch Abraham (pbuh). The fire was finally ready. It was so hot. Birds could not fly over the flames. People of the kingdom tied Abraham’s hands and feet. They placed him on a catapult. A catapult is a machine. People used this machine to throw Abraham (pbuh) into the fire.

vocabulary.definition: Thinking you are better than other people.
A machine for throwing things far away.
The hot, bright parts of a fire that go up into the air.
Feeling bad because you did something wrong.

hotspots.title: The Fire
hotspots.description: The people made a huge and dangerous fire.

hotspots.title: The Catapult
hotspots.description: The people placed Abraham (pbuh) on a catapult to throw him into the fire.

exercises.title: Calm in Danger
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 8.
exercises.question: Abraham was afraid because the fire was very big and dangerous.
exercises.explanation: The fire was dangerous, “But Abraham (pbuh) stayed calm because he trusted Allah. Allah was always with him.”

feedback.correct: Correct! Abraham was not afraid. He stayed calm because he trusted Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 8 again. Find the sentence that starts with “But Abraham (pbuh) stayed …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Too Proud to Say Sorry
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 8. Choose the right answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “But they were too arrogant to accept their mistake.” Did the people accept their mistake?
options: Yes, but only after the fire.
No, they did not accept it.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Too + adjective + to + verb” means that something stops an action. The people were very arrogant, so they did not accept their mistake. Instead, they started shouting.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Too arrogant to accept” means they did not accept it.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first lines of Chapter 8 again. What did the people do after this sentence?

languageFocusExercises.title: So, To, Could Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 8.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit the sentences about the fire?

formChoices.sentence: The fire was [choice] huge that it was dangerous to go near it.
People from many different towns came [choice] Abraham (pbuh).
Birds [choice] fly over the flames.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So + adjective + that …” shows a result: The fire was so huge that it was dangerous. “To + base verb” tells us why people came: to watch. “Could not” shows that the birds were not able to fly over the flames in the past.

feedback.correct: Well done. You completed the result, the purpose and the past ability.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 8 again. Which word goes with “that”? Which small word shows why people came? The story is in the past.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words About Feelings and Actions
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each Chapter 8 expression with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 8 mean?

matchingPairs.right: felt bad about their wrong action

correctAnswer.felt ashamed: felt bad about their wrong action

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The people “felt ashamed” because they knew Abraham was right. Abraham “stayed calm because he trusted Allah”. The people “collected firewood for the fire for days”, and after that time the fire “was finally ready”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You understood the key words of the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Find each expression in Chapter 8 and read the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Describe a Dangerous Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about a very hot day.
languageFocusExercises.question: What could you not do, and what did you do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use a pattern with “too” or “so”, one “could not” sentence, one purpose with “to”, and one time marker.

feedback.correct: Keep the description short and connected.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say how hot it was: “so … that …” or “too … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: The day was so hot that we stayed inside.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you could not do: “We could not …”
discussionPrompts.example: We could not play football in the park.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what for: “We went … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: In the evening, we went to the pool to swim.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say how it ended: “Finally, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Finally, the air was cool, and we went for a walk.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What threw Abraham (pbuh) into the fire?
beforeYouRead.quote: They placed him on a catapult.

I can say that something was too hot or so big that …
I can describe a hot day or a heavy bag.

pages.title: Allah Saves Abraham
pages.content:
They threw him into huge flames. At that moment, Angel Gabriel came to him and asked, “Is there anything you wish for?” Abraham (pbuh) only said, “Nothing from you!” He knew Allah was on his side. Allah told the fire to be cool for Abraham (pbuh). The fire became cool and safe for him. It only burnt the ropes on Abraham’s (pbuh) hands and feet.

He sat in the middle of the fire safely. The fire turned into a garden. Prophet Abraham (pbuh) came out in good condition when the flames cooled. People were shocked to see that Abraham (pbuh) was not harmed at all. The miracle amazed the people, but they did not change their minds. They were still arrogant and rude. Abraham (pbuh) tried hard to show them the truth, but they were still against him.

vocabulary.definition: A wonderful event that only Allah can make happen.
Made someone feel very surprised.
Long, thick strings used for tying things.
A very short time; one point in time.

hotspots.title: The Miracle
hotspots.description: Allah made the fire cool and safe for Abraham (pbuh).

hotspots.title: Angel Gabriel
hotspots.description: Angel Gabriel asked Abraham (pbuh) if he wished for anything, but Abraham trusted only Allah.

exercises.title: In the Fire
exercises.instructions: Match each part with what happened in Chapter 9.
exercises.question: What happened when Abraham was in the fire?

matchingPairs.right: asked, “Is there anything you wish for?”
became cool and safe for Abraham.
were the only things that burnt.
were amazed, but they did not change their minds.

correctAnswer.Angel Gabriel: asked, “Is there anything you wish for?”
correctAnswer.The fire: became cool and safe for Abraham.
correctAnswer.The ropes: were the only things that burnt.
correctAnswer.The people: were amazed, but they did not change their minds.

exercises.explanation: Gabriel asked Abraham what he wished for. Allah told the fire to be cool, and it “only burnt the ropes on Abraham’s (pbuh) hands and feet.” The miracle amazed the people, “but they did not change their minds.”

feedback.correct: Well done! You found what Gabriel, the fire and the people did.
feedback.incorrect: The first paragraph is about Gabriel, the fire and the ropes. The second paragraph tells us about the people.

languageFocusExercises.title: Not Harmed at All
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 9. Then decide: True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “People were shocked to see that Abraham (pbuh) was not harmed at all.” True or false: The fire hurt Abraham a little.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Not … at all” makes a negative stronger. “Not harmed at all” means there was no harm, not even a little. The fire only burnt the ropes on his hands and feet.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Not at all” means not even a little.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the words “at all”. They make “not harmed” stronger. Was there any harm?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Changed and What Did Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What changed, and what did not change?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The fire [blank] cool and safe for him. … The fire [blank] a garden. … Abraham (pbuh) tried hard to show them the truth, but they were [blank] against him.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Became + adjective” (became cool) and “turned into + noun” (turned into a garden) show a change. “Still” shows that a situation did not change: After the miracle, the people were against Abraham, the same as before.

feedback.correct: Well done. The fire changed, but the people did not.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 9 again. “Turned into” goes before a noun. The story is in the past. Which word shows that something continued?

languageFocusExercises.title: Nothing from You
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the lines from Chapter 9. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: Gabriel asked, “Is there anything you wish for?” Abraham (pbuh) only said, “Nothing from you!” What does Abraham mean?
options: He wants many things from Gabriel.
He does not want anything from Gabriel.
He has nothing to give Gabriel.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Anything” is used in questions: “Is there anything …?” “Nothing” means “not anything”. Abraham does not ask Gabriel for help because he knew Allah was on his side.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Nothing from you” means he does not want anything from Gabriel.
feedback.incorrect: Read the next sentence in Chapter 9: “He knew Allah was on his side.” Who did Abraham trust?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Surprising Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about a surprising change.
languageFocusExercises.question: What changed, and what stayed the same?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “became” or “turned into”, one time linker, one reaction, and “still”.

feedback.correct: Make the four sentences form one short situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what changed: “… turned into …” or “… became …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our empty garden turned into a beautiful green place.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say when: “When …” or “At that moment, …”
discussionPrompts.example: When spring came, the first flowers opened.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how someone felt: “… was amazed to see …”
discussionPrompts.example: My little sister was amazed to see the colors.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what did not change: “… is still …”
discussionPrompts.example: But our old tree is still small.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What did the fire turn into?
beforeYouRead.quote: The fire turned into a garden.

I can say what changed and what was still the same.
I can talk about a surprising change in my life.

pages.title: Abraham and Nimrod
pages.content:
Nimrod was the King of Babylon. He heard about the miracle. He thought Abraham was not an ordinary person. So, he wanted to meet him. He called him and asked, “Who is your God?” Abraham (pbuh) said, “He is Allah, the One. He gives life and brings death.” “I can give life and death,” said Nimrod. He ordered his guards to bring two slaves.

Nimrod said, “Kill one of the slaves.” The soldiers killed one of them. Then Nimrod said, “I let the second slave live. Let him go.” The slave was free. “See! I can also give life and death!” Nimrod said to Abraham (pbuh). Abraham (pbuh) said, “Allah makes the sun rise in the east. Can you make the sun rise from the west?” Of course, Nimrod couldn’t do this; only Allah can make the sun rise in the east. This made Nimrod angrier.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:abraham-babylon
__historical_entity__:abraham-nimrod
People who belong to another person and are not free.
Normal; not special.
People whose job is to protect a person or place.
The direction where the sun comes up in the morning.

hotspots.title: Nimrod
hotspots.description: Nimrod claimed that he could give life and death.

hotspots.title: The Sun from the West
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) challenged Nimrod to make the sun rise from the west.

exercises.title: The Sun Question
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 10.
exercises.question: Nimrod said, “I can also give life and death!” How did Abraham show that Nimrod was wrong?
options: He asked Nimrod to let the second slave go free.
He asked Nimrod to make the sun rise from the west.
He asked Nimrod to make the big fire cool down.
exercises.explanation: Abraham said, “Allah makes the sun rise in the east. Can you make the sun rise from the west?” Nimrod could not do this. It was Nimrod himself who let the second slave go.

feedback.correct: Right! Nimrod could not move the sun. Only Allah has this power.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 10 again. What did Abraham ask Nimrod to do?

languageFocusExercises.title: Words from the King’s Palace
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each Chapter 10 expression with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 10 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Nimrod thought Abraham “was not an ordinary person”: he was different from other people. “Let him go” means “allow him to leave”. Abraham says Allah “gives life and brings death”. At the end, Nimrod was already angry, and the question “made Nimrod angrier”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You understood the key words of the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Find each expression in Chapter 10 and read the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Heard, Thought, Wanted
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which past form fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Nimrod was the King of Babylon. He [blank] about the miracle. He [blank] Abraham was not an ordinary person. So, he [blank] to meet him.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story is in the past. “Hear” and “think” are irregular: hear → heard, think → thought (not “thinked”). “Want” is regular: want → wanted. First Nimrod heard, then he thought, so he wanted to meet Abraham.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used the past forms in the right order.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first lines of Chapter 10 again. The past of “think” is not “thinked”.

languageFocusExercises.title: The King’s Order
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to make the sentence from Chapter 10.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Nimrod order?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The pattern is “order + person + to + base verb”: “He ordered his guards to bring two slaves.” First we say who got the order, then what they must do.

feedback.correct: Correct. You built the order: ordered + person + to + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Start with “He ordered”. Then say who got the order, and then “to + verb”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Claim and a Test
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about testing a friend’s words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can your friend really do it?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “thought ...”, “ordered ... to ...”, “Can you ...?”, and “couldn’t ...” or “made ... + adjective”.

feedback.correct: Keep the situation short and connected.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone thought: “My friend thought …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend thought he was the fastest runner in our class.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what someone ordered: “Our teacher told us to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our teacher told us to run to the wall and back.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Ask: “Can you …?”
discussionPrompts.example: I asked him, “Can you run faster than me?”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give the result: “He couldn’t, and …”
discussionPrompts.example: He couldn’t, and this made us both laugh.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Nimrod order his guards to bring?
beforeYouRead.quote: He ordered his guards to bring two slaves.

iCan: I can tell what Abraham (pbuh) asked King Nimrod.
I can say what someone thought and what someone ordered.
I can test a friend’s claim with “Can you …?”.

pages.title: Abraham Leaves Babylon
pages.content:
Only one woman and one man believed in Allah with Abraham (pbuh). The woman’s name was Sarah, and the man’s name was Lot. Lot later became a prophet. Abraham (pbuh) understood that no one was going to listen to him. So, he decided to leave Babylon and travel to other lands to tell people about Allah’s message.

Abraham (pbuh) began his journey. He traveled from Babylon to Syria and Palestine on camels. It was a long, hot, and tiring journey. During his journey, Abraham (pbuh) married Hagar and had a son. They named the baby Ishmael. One day, Allah asked Abraham (pbuh) to travel with his wife and the little child, Ishmael. They all traveled for a long time. Finally, they arrived at a quiet valley near two small hills, Safa and Marwah.

__historical_entity__:abraham-syria-ancient
__historical_entity__:abraham-palestine-ancient
__historical_entity__:abraham-safa-and-marwa-ancient
A long trip from one place to another.

exercises.title: The Long Journey
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 11 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: Abraham decided to leave Babylon.
Abraham married Hagar, and they had a son, Ishmael.
Allah asked Abraham to travel with his wife and the little child.
Abraham, Hagar and Ishmael arrived at a quiet valley near Safa and Marwah.

exercises.explanation: No one was going to listen, so Abraham decided to leave Babylon. During his journey, he married Hagar and had a son, Ishmael. One day, Allah asked him to travel with his wife and the child. Finally, they arrived at a quiet valley near Safa and Marwah.

feedback.correct: Great! You followed the journey from Babylon to the quiet valley.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the time words in Chapter 11: “So”, “During his journey”, “One day” and “Finally”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Talking About a Journey
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each Chapter 11 phrase in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where or how did they travel? When, or how long?

items: from Babylon to Syria and Palestine

Where or how: from Babylon to Syria and Palestine

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “From … to …” gives the start and end of a route, “on camels” tells us how they traveled, and “near” gives a place. “During” and “for a long time” are about time, and “Finally” shows the end of the journey.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated place and travel words from time words.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Does this phrase answer “Where?” or “How?”, or does it answer “When?” or “How long?”

languageFocusExercises.title: Decided To, Asked To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 11.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit each sentence about the journey?

formChoices.sentence: So, he decided [choice] Babylon …
… travel to other lands [choice] people about Allah’s message.
One day, Allah asked Abraham (pbuh) [choice] with his wife and the little child, Ishmael.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “decide”, use “to + base verb”: decided to leave. “To + base verb” can also give a purpose: he traveled to tell people about Allah’s message. After “ask + person”, use “to + base verb”: asked Abraham to travel.

feedback.correct: Well done. All three need “to + base verb”.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 11 again. After “decided”, after “asked Abraham”, and to give a purpose, the chapter uses “to + base verb”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about the journey?

errorItems.sentence: Finally, they arrived to a quiet valley near two small hills, Safa and Marwah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The past form of “begin” is “began”. We say “arrive at” a place, not “arrive to”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You fixed the past verb and the preposition.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 11 again. What is the past of “begin”? Which word comes after “arrived”?

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about a journey you made.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where did you go, and how?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “decided to”, “from ... to ...”, a transport phrase, and “Finally, arrived at ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the journey clear and short.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what you decided: “We decided to …”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give the route: “We traveled from … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We traveled from our city to her small village.

discussionPrompts.example: We went by bus, and the journey took six hours.

discussionPrompts.example: Finally, we arrived at her house in the evening.

pages.title: Hagar and Ishmael in the Valley
pages.content:
Abraham (pbuh) told his wife to stay near one of the hills with Ishmael. Abraham (pbuh) left them there. Hagar knew that this was part of Allah’s plan. She thought fearlessly, “Allah will never let us die; He will surely protect us.” Allah is the best protector. The valley had no fruit, no trees, no food, and no water.

Abraham (pbuh) went away and asked Allah to protect his family. He asked Allah to give them blessings, so they could thank Him. But soon, Hagar and the little child Ishmael had no food or water left. Hagar had to give food to her child. She looked for food and water. She ran from hill to hill. But it was useless. There was no water and nobody to help her.

vocabulary.definition: Good things and help that come from Allah.
In a brave way, without being afraid.
Not bringing any good result.
An idea about what to do and how to do it.

hotspots.title: Hagar’s Trust
hotspots.description: Hagar trusted that Allah would protect her and Ishmael.

hotspots.title: The Empty Valley
hotspots.description: The valley had no food, trees, fruit, or water.

exercises.title: Hagar’s Trust
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 12.
exercises.question: Abraham left Hagar and Ishmael in the valley. Why was Hagar not afraid?
options: The valley had a lot of fruit trees and fresh water for her and her baby.
She knew it was part of Allah’s plan, and she believed Allah would protect them.
Sarah and Lot were there with her, and they helped her with the baby.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 12 says Hagar “knew that this was part of Allah’s plan.” She thought fearlessly, “Allah will never let us die; He will surely protect us.” The valley had no fruit, no trees, no food and no water.

feedback.correct: Yes! Hagar trusted Allah. Then, when the food and water were gone, she still worked hard and searched.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 12 again. What did Hagar know, and what did she think?

languageFocusExercises.title: Words from the Valley
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each Chapter 12 word with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 12 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Hagar “thought fearlessly”: she was not afraid. Abraham “asked Allah to protect his family” and “to give them blessings”. Hagar ran from hill to hill, “but it was useless”: running did not help her find water.

feedback.correct: Well done. You understood the key words of the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Find each word in Chapter 12 and read the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Hagar’s Strong Belief
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to build Hagar’s words from Chapter 12.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where does “never” go in a sentence with “will”?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Never” goes after “will” and before the main verb: will never let. “Let + person + base verb” means “allow”: let us die. Hagar is sure about the future: Allah will protect them.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Will never let us die” shows Hagar’s strong belief.
feedback.incorrect: Start with “Allah will”. Put “never” before the verb “let”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Told To, Had To, Nobody
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 12.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit the sentences about Hagar?

formChoices.sentence: Abraham (pbuh) told his wife [choice] near one of the hills with Ishmael.
Hagar [choice] give food to her child.
There was no water and [choice] to help her.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Tell + person + to + base verb” gives an instruction: told his wife to stay. “Had to” shows a duty in the past. “Nobody” means “no person”: there was no water and no person to help her.

feedback.correct: Well done. You completed the instruction, the duty and the sentence about no help.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 12 again. The story is in the past. Which word means “no person”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Need, Request and Action
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about something your class needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did you need, and what did you do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “no ...”, “had to ...”, “asked ... to ...”, and “will surely/will never ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the four ideas connected.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what is missing: “We had no … left.”
discussionPrompts.example: Our class had no paper left for the project.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you had to do: “We had to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We had to finish our poster by Friday.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Ask for help: “We asked … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We asked our teacher to give us some paper.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what will happen: “We will surely …”
discussionPrompts.example: We will surely finish the poster on time.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What did the valley have?
beforeYouRead.quote: The valley had no fruit, no trees, no food, and no water.

iCan: I can tell what Hagar did in the empty valley.
I can say what was missing and what someone had to do.
I can describe a school need and ask for help.

pages.title: The Zamzam Water
pages.content:
Hagar was running in the desert and Ishmael was crying for water. Suddenly water came out of the ground under Ishmael’s feet. When Hagar saw this, she shouted, “Zamzam!” It means “Flow slowly, stop!” She was so happy. She drank the water. Then she took some water in her hands and gave it to Ishmael.

Later, this water became very famous. It is still there today. The water is special because it was a gift from Allah in the middle of the desert. Ishmael and his mother began to live near the Zamzam water. More people came there because of this water. They built a city called Mecca.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:abraham-mecca-valley-ancient
__historical_entity__:abraham-zamzam
A very dry place with little water and few plants.
Quickly and when you do not expect it.
Said something in a very loud voice.
Known by many people.

hotspots.title: Water from the Ground
hotspots.description: Water came out of the ground under Ishmael’s feet.

hotspots.title: Mecca
hotspots.description: People came because of the water and built a city called Mecca.

exercises.title: A New City
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 13.
exercises.question: Why did more people come to this place in the desert?
options: The hills of Safa and Marwah had fruit trees.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13 says: “More people came there because of this water. They built a city called Mecca.” The Ka’ba comes later, in Chapter 14.

feedback.correct: Right! The water was a gift from Allah. Because of it, people came and built Mecca.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentences of Chapter 13 again. Find the words “because of …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Going On, or One Moment?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part of Chapter 13 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Was it going on, or did it happen at one moment?

items: Hagar was running in the desert
Suddenly water came out of the ground

Was going on: Hagar was running in the desert
Happened at one moment: Suddenly water came out of the ground

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Was + -ing” (was running, was crying) tells us what was going on in the background. The past simple (came, shouted, drank) tells us what happened at one moment. “Suddenly” shows a surprising new event.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the background actions from the events.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs. “Was running” and “was crying” were going on. “Came”, “shouted” and “drank” happened at one moment.

languageFocusExercises.title: Because or Because Of?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 13.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which fits: became, because or because of?

formChoices.sentence: Later, this water [choice] very famous.
The water is special [choice] it was a gift from Allah in the middle of the desert.
More people came there [choice] this water.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Became” is the past of “become” and shows a change. “Because” comes before a subject and verb (it was a gift …). “Because of” comes before a noun (this water).

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose “because” before a clause and “because of” before a noun.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the words after the gap. Is there a subject and verb (it was …), or only a noun (this water)?

languageFocusExercises.title: Words That Tell Someone What to Do
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the lines from Chapter 13. Choose the right answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: When Hagar saw this, she shouted, “Zamzam!” It means “Flow slowly, stop!” What do the words “Flow” and “stop” do here?
options: They tell what happened in the past.
They ask the water a question.
They tell the water what to do.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Flow” and “stop” are imperatives: Base verbs that tell someone or something what to do. There is no subject before them.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Flow slowly, stop!” tells the water what to do.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs “Flow” and “stop”. Is there a question mark? Is there a past form?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Sudden Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about something that happened suddenly.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened suddenly?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use “was/were + -ing”, “Suddenly ...”, “Then ...”, and “because ...”.

feedback.correct: Make the sequence short and clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what was going on: “I was …ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: I was doing my homework in my room.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Add a sudden event: “Suddenly, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Suddenly, the lights went out.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what happened next: “Then …”
discussionPrompts.example: Then my father brought a candle.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give a reason: “… because …”
discussionPrompts.example: I was happy because I could finish my homework.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did people build near the water?
beforeYouRead.quote: They built a city called Mecca.

iCan: I can tell how the Zamzam water came out of the ground.
I can say what was happening when something suddenly changed.
I can tell a short true story with “Suddenly”.

pages.title: The Ka’ba and Abraham’s Message
pages.content:
During that time, Abraham (pbuh) visited Mecca several times to see his family. One day, Allah asked Abraham (pbuh) to build the House of Allah, the Ka’ba. Abraham (pbuh) said to Ishmael, “O Ishmael, Allah gave me an important job, and you will help me with it.” Ishmael said, “I will help you for sure.” The Ka’ba was a very old building. It was the first holy place on Earth, but it was lost after a long time.

Father and son found the bottom of the old building of the Ka’ba and built the new building on it. After Abraham (pbuh) built the Sacred Ka’ba, his mission was over. He built a special place for Muslims of all colors. Today, people still visit the House of Allah to make Hajj. Hajj makes us remember Abraham (pbuh) and his family’s story.

After many years, Ishmael’s family grew and grew. One of them was Muhammad, the Prophet of Islam (pbuh). Muhammad (pbuh) told people the message of his ancestor, Abraham (pbuh).

The message is: “There is no god but Allah. He has no partner, rival or helper. Allah is unique in every way.”

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:abraham-mecca-valley-ancient
__historical_entity__:abraham-kaaba-abraham
An important job that someone must do.
A person in your family who lived a long time before you.
Someone who shares something, like work or power, with another person.
Special because it is connected with God or religion.

hotspots.title: Building the Ka’ba
hotspots.description: Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael built the House of Allah.

hotspots.title: Hajj
hotspots.description: People still visit the House of Allah for Hajj.

exercises.title: The Ka’ba and the Message
exercises.instructions: Match each part with what Chapter 14 says about it.
exercises.question: What does Chapter 14 tell us?

matchingPairs.right: said, “I will help you for sure.”
was the first holy place on Earth.
makes us remember Abraham and his family.
told people the message of his ancestor.

correctAnswer.Ishmael: said, “I will help you for sure.”
correctAnswer.The Ka’ba: was the first holy place on Earth.
correctAnswer.Hajj: makes us remember Abraham and his family.
correctAnswer.Muhammad (pbuh): told people the message of his ancestor.

exercises.explanation: Ishmael promised to help his father. The Ka’ba “was the first holy place on Earth”. “Hajj makes us remember Abraham (pbuh) and his family’s story.” Muhammad (pbuh) told people Abraham’s message: “There is no god but Allah.”

feedback.correct: Well done! You connected the building of the Ka’ba with Hajj and the message.
feedback.incorrect: The first paragraph is about Ishmael and the Ka’ba. The next paragraphs tell us about Hajj and Muhammad (pbuh).

languageFocusExercises.title: A Promise to Help
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Ishmael’s answer from Chapter 14. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: Abraham said, “Allah gave me an important job, and you will help me with it.” Ishmael said, “I will help you for sure.” What does Ishmael mean?
options: He promises to help his father.
He is not sure he can help.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Will + base verb” can make a promise about the future. “For sure” means “certainly”, so Ishmael is very sure: He will help.

feedback.correct: Correct. “I will help you for sure” is a promise.
feedback.incorrect: Look at “will” and “for sure”. Is Ishmael talking about the past or the future? Is he sure?

languageFocusExercises.title: Which Question Does It Answer?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each part of the sentence with the question it answers.
languageFocusExercises.question: “During that time, Abraham (pbuh) visited Mecca several times to see his family.”
languageFocusExercises.explanation: One sentence can answer many questions. “During that time” gives the time, “Mecca” gives the place, “several times” means more than two times, and “to + base verb” (to see) gives the reason or purpose.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the time, place, number of times and purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentence of Chapter 14 again. Which part tells the purpose? Which part tells how many times?

languageFocusExercises.title: After, Still, One Of
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] Abraham (pbuh) built the Sacred Ka’ba, his mission was over. … Today, people [blank] visit the House of Allah to make Hajj. … After many years, Ishmael’s family grew and grew. [blank] them was Muhammad, the Prophet of Islam (pbuh).
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After + past event” shows what came first: First he built the Ka’ba, then his mission was over. “Still” shows that something continues today. “One of + plural” picks one person from a group.

feedback.correct: Correct. You connected the past, today and the Prophet’s family.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 14 again. When was the mission over: Before or after the building? Which word shows that Hajj continues today?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Shared Task
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about a job your class did together.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did you do, and why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use one time expression, purpose with “to”, “will” for help, and “still” for continuation.

feedback.correct: Keep the four ideas connected.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Begin with the time: “Last week, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last week, our class had a big job: Cleaning the school garden.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what for: “We … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We collected the rubbish to make the garden beautiful.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Add a promise: “I will help you …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend said, “I will help you for sure.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what still happens: “Today, we still …”
discussionPrompts.example: Today, we still water the plants every Friday.

options: the bottom of the old Ka’ba
beforeYouRead.quote: Father and son found the bottom of the old building of the Ka’ba

roles.name: Map Maker
roles.job: You draw a simple map with four places: Babylon, Syria and Palestine, the valley near Safa and Marwah, and Mecca.

For each place, copy one sentence from the book, for example: “They built a city called Mecca.”
For each place, add one sentence of your own with a pattern like “decided to …”, “Suddenly, …” or “still …”.
Practise a two-minute presentation; each member says one part.
