groupTask.solo: Make a small map alone with the four places, one sentence from the book and one sentence of your own for each place.

legend.route:toSyriaPalestine: From Babylon to Syria and Palestine
legend.route:toValley: To the valley of Safa and Marwah

places.name: Babylon
places.text: Babylon was an old kingdom in Mesopotamia. Abraham (pbuh) was born here a very long time ago. Nimrod was the King of Babylon.
places.teacherNote: The book gives no year. It says only “a very long time ago”. It does not name Abraham’s (pbuh) town; the pin marks the old city of Babylon.
places.question: Who was the King of Babylon?

places.name: Mesopotamia
places.text: Mesopotamia was an old land between two rivers. The kingdom of Babylon was in Mesopotamia.
places.teacherNote: The two rivers are the Tigris and the Euphrates; the A2 story does not name them. The circle is only approximate. There were no fixed borders.
places.question: Which kingdom was in Mesopotamia?

places.name: The fire
places.text: The people of the kingdom collected firewood for days and made a huge fire. They threw Abraham (pbuh) into it. Allah told the fire to be cool, and Abraham (pbuh) came out safe.
places.teacherNote: The book does not say where the fire was. It says only that the people of the kingdom made it, so the pin beside Babylon just shows the event. After the miracle, King Nimrod met Abraham (pbuh) (chapter 10).
places.question: Why did Abraham (pbuh) stay calm near the fire?

places.name: Syria / al-Sham
places.text: Syria, or al-Sham, was a land west of Mesopotamia. Abraham (pbuh) traveled there after Babylon. He traveled on camels.
places.teacherNote: Old al-Sham was larger than the country of Syria today. The circle is approximate. The Arabic edition says بلاد الشام.
places.question: How did Abraham (pbuh) travel from Babylon?

places.name: Palestine
places.text: Palestine was a land near the Mediterranean Sea. Abraham (pbuh) traveled there on his journey. It was a long, hot and tiring journey.
places.teacherNote: The book says that Abraham (pbuh) married Hagar and had his son Ishmael “during his journey”, but it does not say where.
places.question: Was the journey easy? Why not?

places.name: Mecca
places.text: This was a quiet valley near two small hills, Safa and Marwah. Here, Zamzam water came out of the ground, and people built the city of Mecca. Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael built the Ka’ba here.
places.teacherNote: The book does not say where the family started this journey; the line is drawn from the Palestine area. Abraham (pbuh) visited Mecca several times, but the book does not say where he came from. The Ka’ba was the first holy place on Earth, and people still visit it for Hajj.
places.question: What does “Zamzam” mean?

challenge.prompt: Find Babylon. Abraham (pbuh) was born in this kingdom.
Find Mesopotamia, the old land between two rivers.
Find Syria (al-Sham). Abraham (pbuh) went there from Babylon on camels.
Find Palestine. It is near the Mediterranean Sea.
Find Mecca. Zamzam water is there, in the desert.

pages.title: Knowledge Check
pages.content: Test your understanding of the major events in Prophet Abraham’s life.

exercises.title: The Little Boy and the Idols
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: What did young Abraham do with his father’s idols?
options: He gave them presents every day.
He played with them like toys.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “But Abraham played with these idols as toys. He rode on their backs and sometimes kicked them.”

feedback.correct: Yes! For Abraham they were only toys. He rode on their backs and sometimes kicked them.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. His father gave the idols presents and asked them for help. Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2: what did Abraham do?

exercises.title: Abraham Talks to His Father
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Abraham’s father was happy when Abraham asked him to stop worshipping stones.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “O my father, follow me: I will guide you on the right way. Stop worshipping stones.” His father got angry and said, “Are you against my gods?”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. His father got angry and asked, “Are you against my gods?”
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 4 again. How did his father feel after Abraham’s words?

exercises.title: “Leave Here Now”
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Abraham’s father said, “Leave here now.” How did Abraham feel?
options: He was glad to leave home and his father.
He was angry and shouted at his father.
He was very sad about his father.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “If you do not stop speaking like this, I will stone you. Leave here now.” Prophet Abraham (pbuh) was very sad about his father.

feedback.correct: Yes. Abraham loved his father, so he was very sad. But he did not stop telling people about Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the first lines of Chapter 5 again. How did Abraham feel about his father?

exercises.title: Food for the Idols
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Abraham asked the idols, “Why don’t you eat the food?” Why did he ask this?
options: He was joking because stone cannot eat.
He was worried that they were hungry.
He wanted to eat the food himself.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “Abraham (pbuh) jokingly asked them, “Why don’t you eat the food? It is getting cold.””

feedback.correct: Yes! He asked jokingly. Stone gods cannot eat, and this shows how silly it was to give them food.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the word “jokingly” in the second paragraph of Chapter 6. Can a stone object eat?

exercises.title: The People Knew
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: The people felt ashamed because they knew Abraham was right.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the grammar patterns and language functions from all fourteen chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Going On, or One Event?
exercises.instructions: Put each part in the right group.
exercises.question: Did it go on for some time, or happen once?

items: Abraham used to watch his father making idols from stone
He was trying to show them the right way
Hagar was running in the desert
One day, his father saw Abraham.
Abraham (pbuh) got an axe and waited.
Suddenly water came out of the ground

Going on for some time: Abraham used to watch his father making idols from stone
He was trying to show them the right way
Hagar was running in the desert
Happened once: One day, his father saw Abraham.
Abraham (pbuh) got an axe and waited.
Suddenly water came out of the ground

exercises.explanation: “Used to + base verb” (used to watch) is a habit in the past: it happened again and again. “Was + -ing” (was trying, was running) is an action that was going on at that time. The past simple (saw, got, came) tells one finished event. Words like “One day” and “Suddenly” often come before one event.

feedback.correct: Well done. Used to and was + -ing go on for some time; the past simple tells one event.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb: used to …? was + -ing? Or one past form like saw or came?

exercises.title: Look: Had To, Could Not, Can, Will
exercises.instructions: Match each sentence from the book with its meaning.
exercises.question: What do had to, could not, can and will mean?

matchingPairs.left: From then on, he had to guide his people.
Birds could not fly over the flames.
matchingPairs.right: In the past, they were not able to do it.

matchingPairs.left: Ask it if it can speak!
matchingPairs.right: Is it able to do this now?

matchingPairs.left: I will help you for sure.

In the past, they were not able to do it.
correctAnswer.Ask it if it can speak!: Is it able to do this now?

exercises.explanation: “Had to + base verb” is a duty in the past: Abraham had to guide his people. “Could not + base verb” means that someone or something was not able to do it in the past. “Can” is about ability now: Abraham asks the people to see if the idol can speak. “Will + base verb” talks about the future, and Ishmael’s “for sure” makes it a promise. After all these words, use the base verb: guide, fly, speak, help.

feedback.correct: Correct. Had to is a duty, could not and can are about ability, and will is a promise.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the small word before the verb: had to, could not, can or will. Is it about a duty, ability or the future?

exercises.title: Look: Because and So
exercises.instructions: Read the two sentences. Then choose the best answer.
exercises.question: Chapter 8: “But Abraham (pbuh) stayed calm because he trusted Allah.” Chapter 10: “He thought Abraham was not an ordinary person. So, he wanted to meet him.” Which parts give the REASON?
options: he stayed calm … / he wanted to meet him
he trusted Allah … / He thought Abraham was not an ordinary person
he stayed calm … / He thought Abraham was not an ordinary person
exercises.explanation: “Because” comes before the reason: Why did Abraham stay calm? Because he trusted Allah. “So” comes before the result: First the reason (Nimrod thought Abraham was not ordinary), then “So, …” and what happened (he wanted to meet him). “Because of” is different: It comes before a noun, not a sentence.

feedback.correct: Correct. Because + the reason; the reason + So + the result.
feedback.incorrect: Ask “Why?” for each sentence. Why did Abraham stay calm? Why did Nimrod want to meet him?

exercises.title: Practise: Reason, Result, Different Idea
exercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: People said, “We saw our fathers worship them; [blank] this, we do the same.” … But they were [blank] arrogant to accept their mistake. … Abraham (pbuh) understood that no one was going to listen to him. [blank], he decided to leave Babylon … It was the first holy place on Earth, [blank] it was lost after a long time.
exercises.explanation: “Because of” comes before a noun or “this”: because of this (not “because this”). “Too + adjective + to + verb” shows a result: they were very arrogant, so they did not accept their mistake. We cannot say very arrogant to. “So” gives the result: No one was going to listen, so he decided to leave. “But” gives a different idea: It was the first holy place, but it was lost.

feedback.correct: Well done. You linked reasons, a result and a different idea.
feedback.incorrect: For each gap, ask: Is the next part a reason, a result or a different idea? Look at the words after each gap: a noun (this), an adjective + to (arrogant to …) or a new sentence?

exercises.title: Practise: Told, Let, Began
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from the book.
exercises.question: Which form comes after “told … not”, “let” and “began”?

formChoices.sentence: He got angry and told his son not [choice] with it again.
Then Nimrod said, “I let the second slave [choice]. Let him go.”
Abraham (pbuh) began [choice] the stone gods, one after another.

exercises.explanation: “Tell + person + (not) to + base verb” gives an instruction: told his son not to play. “Let + person + base verb” (no “to”) means “allow”: let the second slave live. After “begin”, use “to + base verb”: began to break.

feedback.correct: Correct. Told … not to + verb; let + base verb; began to + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb before the gap: told, let or began. Only one of them takes the base verb without “to”. Check Chapters 2, 6 and 10.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Mistake
exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
exercises.question: Can you fix the verbs in these sentences?

errorItems.sentence: If you will not stop speaking like this, I will stone you.
People found Abraham (pbuh) and bringed him to the house of idols.
She was so happy. She drinked the water.

exercises.explanation: After “If”, use the present, not “will”: “If you do not stop …, I will …”. “Will” goes only in the result part. “Bring” and “drink” change in the past: brought, drank (not bringed, drinked).

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed all three sentences.
feedback.incorrect: Compare with the book: Chapter 5 (the father’s words), Chapter 7 (People found Abraham …) and Chapter 13 (Hagar and the water).

exercises.title: Practise: Still Against Him
exercises.instructions: Put the words in order to make the sentence from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: How do we say that something did not change?
exercises.explanation: “Still” shows that a situation did not change: Before the miracle and after it, the people were against Abraham. “Still” comes after “was/were”: they were still against him. Compare a change in the same chapter: “The fire became cool and safe for him.” “Tried hard to + verb” shows a big effort.

feedback.correct: Well done. They were still against him: No change.
feedback.incorrect: Start with what Abraham tried to do. Then use “but” and say what did not change. “Still” comes after “were”.

exercises.title: Use: A Rainy Afternoon
exercises.instructions: Complete this new text from the bank. Two words are extra.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a school story?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Last Friday, it was raining when school finished. Our teacher told us [blank] wait inside [blank] we had no umbrellas. We [blank] wait for thirty minutes. Then the sky became clear, but the ground was [blank] wet. We walked home carefully.
exercises.explanation: “Told us to wait” gives an instruction. “Because” + a sentence gives the reason: we had no umbrellas. “Had to” shows what was necessary on that day (“used to” is for a habit, not one day). “Still” shows no change: The sky changed, but the ground was still wet.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new place.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each gap: An instruction? a reason? something necessary on one day? no change?

exercises.title: Use: A Day I Remember
exercises.instructions: Write 4–5 sentences about a hard day. Tell a partner first.
exercises.question: Can you tell the story of a hard day?
exercises.explanation: Example: “Last winter, I was walking to school with my brother. Suddenly, it started to snow. We could not see the road, so we had to walk slowly. My mother told us to wear our warm coats. Now it is spring, but I still remember that day.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: was + -ing, one past event, could not / had to, so or because, told … to, still.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Set the scene: “Last …, I was …ing when …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last winter, I was walking to school when it started to snow.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what happened: “One day / Suddenly, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Suddenly, I saw a small cat under a car.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what you had to do: “I could not …, so I had to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I could not leave it there, so I had to carry it home.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — End with: “My … told me to … . I still …”
discussionPrompts.example: My mother told me to give it some milk. I still look after the cat.

options: Allah makes Abraham the king of Babylon one day.
Allah gives Abraham food and drink and heals him.
Allah sends Abraham gold and a big house in the city.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 5 Abraham says: “My Lord gives me food and drink when I need them. He heals me when I am sick. Your gods have no power to do these things.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Abraham showed the difference: Allah helps him, but the stone gods have no power.
feedback.incorrect: Read Abraham’s last words to the people in Chapter 5. What does Allah give him?

exercises.title: The Largest Idol

exercises.question: Abraham broke all the stone gods, even the largest one.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “He left the largest one unbroken. Abraham (pbuh) placed the axe around its neck and hurried back home.”

feedback.correct: Right. He did not break the largest one. He put the axe around its neck.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 6. What did Abraham do with the largest stone god?

exercises.title: Abraham’s Life in Order
exercises.instructions: Put these events in the correct order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and later in Abraham’s life?

sequencingItems.text: Abraham talks to King Nimrod about the sun.
Abraham looks at the star, the moon and the sun.
Abraham and Ishmael build the Ka’ba.
The people throw Abraham into the fire.
Water comes out of the ground under Ishmael’s feet.
Abraham breaks the stone gods.

exercises.explanation: The sky (Chapters 3–4), the broken idols (Chapter 6), the fire (Chapters 8–9), Nimrod (Chapter 10), the Zamzam water (Chapter 13) and the Ka’ba (Chapter 14).

feedback.correct: Yes. The story moves from Babylon to the valley where Mecca was built.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the night in the cave. Remember: Nimrod heard about Abraham after the miracle of the fire.

exercises.title: Places in the Story
exercises.instructions: Match each place with what happened there.
exercises.question: What happened in each place?

matchingPairs.right: Abraham thought about Allah and looked at the sky.

matchingPairs.left: the big house of the stone gods
matchingPairs.right: Abraham broke the idols with an axe.
Abraham and Ishmael built the House of Allah.

correctAnswer.a cave on a mountain: Abraham thought about Allah and looked at the sky.
correctAnswer.the big house of the stone gods: Abraham broke the idols with an axe.
correctAnswer.Mecca: Abraham and Ishmael built the House of Allah.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “he found a cave and sat there. He started thinking about Allah.” Chapter 6: “he went into the big house full of human-like objects.” Chapter 10: “Nimrod was the King of Babylon.” Chapter 14: “Abraham (pbuh) visited Mecca several times”, and there he built the Ka’ba with Ishmael.

feedback.correct: Yes. The story starts in Babylon and ends in Mecca.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapters 3, 6, 10 and 14. Where was Abraham in each one?

exercises.title: Too Proud
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from Chapter 8.
exercises.question: The people knew Abraham was right. Why didn’t they accept their mistake?
options: They did not hear his words.
The king told them to stop.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 says: “They felt ashamed and looked at each other because they knew Abraham was right. But they were too arrogant to accept their mistake.”

feedback.correct: Yes. They knew the truth, but their pride stopped them.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first two sentences of Chapter 8. Which word explains why they did not change?

exercises.title: A Gift in the Desert
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 13 with one word: gift, price or river.
exercises.question: Why is the Zamzam water special?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The water is special because it was a [blank] from Allah in the middle of the desert.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13 says: “The water is special because it was a gift from Allah in the middle of the desert.” Before that, “The valley had no fruit, no trees, no food, and no water.”

feedback.correct: Yes. In a dry valley with no water, the water came from Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 13. What was the water from Allah?

exercises.title: Leaving Babylon
exercises.instructions: Is this sentence true or false?
exercises.question: Abraham left Babylon because he understood that no one was going to listen to him.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 11 says: “Abraham (pbuh) understood that no one was going to listen to him. So, he decided to leave Babylon and travel to other lands to tell people about Allah’s message.”

feedback.correct: True. He left Babylon to take Allah’s message to other lands.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 11. Find the word “So”. What came before it?

exercises.title: Abraham’s Family and Friends
exercises.instructions: Match each person with the right sentence.
exercises.question: What does the story tell us about each person?

matchingPairs.right: She believed in Allah with Abraham in Babylon.
She ran from hill to hill to find water.
Water came out of the ground under his feet.

correctAnswer.Sarah: She believed in Allah with Abraham in Babylon.
correctAnswer.Hagar: She ran from hill to hill to find water.
correctAnswer.Ishmael: Water came out of the ground under his feet.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 11: “The woman’s name was Sarah, and the man’s name was Lot. Lot later became a prophet.” Chapter 12: Hagar “ran from hill to hill.” Chapter 13: “Suddenly water came out of the ground under Ishmael’s feet.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Each of these people helps Abraham’s story go on.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the start of Chapter 11, the end of Chapter 12 and the start of Chapter 13.

exercises.title: Abraham’s Message
exercises.instructions: Choose the message from Chapter 14.
exercises.question: Which message does Abraham’s story end with?
options: Every town should have its own god and its own temple.
People should follow their fathers’ way and their old gods.
There is no god but Allah, and He has no partner.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 14 ends with the message: “There is no god but Allah. He has no partner, rival or helper. Allah is unique in every way.”

feedback.correct: Yes. This is the same message Abraham told his father and his people.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 14. What is the message?
